issues: What is the legal test for determining whether an activity constitutes a 'source of income' for tax purposes, as opposed to a personal hobby or non-commercial pursuit
Whether losses from an activity conducted without a reasonable expectation of profit can be deducted from other income
What factors distinguish a business carried on with a view to profit from a personal endeavour lacking commercial character
Whether the 'reasonable expectation of profit' test survives as a standalone legal test or has been replaced by an objective 'pursuit of profit' inquiry
key_facts: Client operated a small side business
The business incurred losses for several consecutive years
Client deducted the business losses against other income
CRA reassessed the taxpayer on the basis the activity was a hobby, not a source of income
causes_of_action: Appeal of CRA reassessment disallowing business loss deductions
Dispute over characterization of activity as a source of income under the Income Tax Act
